title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
description:
Given the head of a nonempty singly linked chain and a positive integer n, remove the node that is n positions from the end. The tail is position 1. Return the head of the resulting chain, even if the removed node was the original head. If no nodes remain, return a null head (null output).

The integer is guaranteed to be no larger than the chain length. Keep all other nodes in their original relative order; repeated values identify separate nodes, so the choice is positional rather than value-based. For a chain of length five, n = 2 removes the fourth node.

This problem is interesting because a singly linked node cannot step backwards. Holding two pointers exactly n nodes apart allows the leading pointer to find the end while the trailing one arrives just before the node to unlink. A dummy predecessor makes deletion of the head follow the same pattern.

Example 1:

Input: head = [1,2,3,4,5], n = 2
Output: [1,2,3,5]

Example 2:

Input: head = [1], n = 1
Output: null

Example 3:

Input: head = [1,2,3], n = 3
Output: [2,3]

Constraints:

  • 1 <= number of nodes <= 5,000.
  • 1 <= n <= number of nodes.
  • -1,000 <= node.val <= 1,000.
